name: Primary Orthostatic Disorder

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Criteria for Primary Orthostatic Hypotension

criteria.description: Sustained reduction of systolic blood pressure of at least 20 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure of at least 10 mmHg within 3 minutes of standing
Exclusion of secondary causes of orthostatic hypotension such as medication effects, dehydration, or systemic illness
Presence of symptoms related to orthostatic intolerance including dizziness, lightheadedness, or syncope on standing
Autonomic function tests showing impaired sympathetic vasoconstriction without evidence of peripheral neuropathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria must be met: documented orthostatic blood pressure drop, exclusion of secondary causes, and presence of orthostatic symptoms.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires careful exclusion of secondary causes and confirmation by autonomic testing.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Orthostatic hypotension with sustained blood pressure drop
searchTerms: sustained drop in blood pressure upright
dizziness caused by nerve issues on standing
fatigue related to low blood pressure on standing

occasional.symptomName: Cognitive slowing or brain fog on standing

searchTerms: muscle weakness in upper back and neck
feeling sick related to standing up
cold hands and feet when standing
seeing black spots or darkness temporarily

rare.symptomName: Transient hearing loss during orthostatic episodes

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests excluding anemia or dehydration
Exclusion of secondary causes via metabolic panels
imaging: Brain MRI typically normal; used to exclude central causes
genetic: No known specific genetic markers identified
other: Autonomic function testing showing impaired sympathetic vasoconstriction
Tilt-table test demonstrating orthostatic hypotension without secondary cause

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of identifiable secondary cause such as medication, dehydration, or systemic illness
Improvement after treatment of underlying cause
Progressive autonomic failure with additional features such as anhidrosis
Abnormal autonomic testing with widespread autonomic dysfunction

redFlags: Presence of neurological deficits beyond orthostatic intolerance
Signs of systemic illness or dehydration
references: Freeman R. Clinical practice. Neurogenic orthostatic hypotension. N Engl J Med. 2008;358(6):615-624.
Low PA. Diagnosis and treatment of neurogenic orthostatic hypotension. Neurology. 2008;71(15):1200-1206.
